thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Lower as Trade Tensions Persist Following APEC Summit

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Lower as Trade Tensions Persist Following APEC Summit
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Monday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.8%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.3%
VelocityShares 3x Inverse Natural Gas ETN ( DGAZ ): -10.5%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -0.5%
iShares China Large-Cap ETF ( FXI ): -0.7%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 0.5%.
US stock futures were in the negative ahead of the opening bell as trade tensions continued to rattle markets following the conclusion of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Papua New Guinea on Sunday, as disagreements over trade prevented the leaders from 21 countries from agreeing on a formal joint statement.
All leaders were in agreement except China, according to a CNN report. China had reportedly felt that it was "singled out" because of references to " unfair trade practices" in the drafted formal joint statement. The phrase has been consistently used as criticism against China by the Trump administration.
Looking ahead to the lone economic data release for Monday, the home builders' index for the month of November will be released at 10 am ET.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.3% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) fell nearly 2% following a Wall Street Journal report that said the company has trimmed production orders for its three recently released iPhone models as the technology company grapples with lower-than-expected demand for the devices. The Wall Street Journal report cited people familiar with the matter. The company had previously projected lower-than-expected sales for the December quarter, causing suppliers to issue warnings that pointed to tepid demand for the new iPhone models. Apple trimmed its production order for the iPhone XR by up to a third of the nearly 70 million handsets some suppliers had been asked to produce between September and February. The production plan for that particular model has once again been lowered as recently as last week, the Journal said.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs (XLF) was flat in pre-market trade. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 1.1% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 0.5%.
Deutsche Bank AG (DB) was down 0.4% after it unveiled a public tender offer with a target acceptance volume of EUR1.0 billion ($1.14 billion) of Euro-denominated senior non-preferred securities. The German banking giant said that the public tender offer, which is set to expire on Nov. 27, is designed to help optimize its future interest payments and maturity structure by taking advantage of a strong liquidity position. Liquidity reserves stood at EUR268 billion as of Sept. 30, the lender said.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was quiet and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.3%.
American depositary receipts of Petroleo Brasileiro SA, known as Petrobras (PBR) rose nearly 2% after media reports said the company is expected to name economist Roberto Castello Branco as its CEO. Branco, who previously served as a board member of the country's central bank and an executive at mining firm Vale (VALE), has agreed to the invitation to become the head of the Brazilian state energy firm, according to a statement from incoming Economy Minister Paulo Guedes released early Monday.
Commodities
Crude was down 1.4%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 1.8%. Natural gas was up 6.8% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 2.9%.
Gold was down 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.2%. Silver was down 0.2%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.3%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were inactive.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were also flat in pre-market trade.
Spectrum Brands (SPB) reported fiscal Q4 adjusted earnings of $0.79 per share, down from $0.85 in the same period a year ago and missing the estimate of $1.08 from analysts polled by CapIQ. For the quarter ended Sept. 30, total revenue of $787.8 million was flat compared with a year ago and below the Street projection of $803.7 million.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up fractionally and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were quiet. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) slipped 0.2% lower.
Gilead Sciences (GILD) rose 0.4% after it said Sunday the China National Medical Products Administration has approved Vemlidy, the company's once-daily treatment for chronic hepatitis B in adults and adolescents. According to Gilead, the drug has demonstrated antiviral efficacy similar to Viread 300 mg but at one-tenth of the dose. The company also cited results of clinical studies that showed how Vemlidy improved renal and bone laboratory safety parameters compared to Viread.
